hypothesis: H1 - Dilatational stepover / relay-ramp structural prior: in Basin-and-Range extension, concealed geothermal faults concentrate where en-echelon normal fault segments step over or relay (<2 km step-overs). These zones are dilational permeability conduits and are commonly missing from mapped Quaternary fault catalogues, which trace through-going scarps rather than the subtle offsets between them.
mechanism: Build a fault-probability prior as Gaussian-smoothed distance to synthetic fault segments (NNE-striking, Basin-and-Range typical), with amplitude boosted in dilatational stepover/relay zones (segment endpoint pairs < 2 km apart, boost sigma 600 m, amplitude 0.85) over a low diffuse background (0.02) with a gentle structural-corridor bump toward the grid centre. Deterministic, seeded (seed 0x9f4e2a), fully reproducible. Raster: 601x601, EPSG:32611 (UTM 11N), 100 m, float32, values clipped to [0,1].
named_non_fault_mimic_process: Erosional / depositional topographic lineations and alluvial-fan or playa shoreline alignments can produce elongated linear anomalies in DEM/radiometric data that look like faults but are not displacement structures; magnetic lineations from mafic dikes or lithologic contacts can mimic fault traces without seismic slip. The prior targets dilatational geometry specifically to reduce this mimicry.
